2607.02494.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
2607.02494.paper_summary: Models trained via Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) serve as the foundational vision encoders for most modern Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs). Despite their widespread adoption, CLIP models exhibit a critical yet underexplored failure mode: irrelevant text appearing within images confounds visual representations, biasing them toward lexical meaning rather than true visual semantics. This robustness issue, commonly described as a Typographic Attack (TA), exposes a vulnerability that poses a significant risk to safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving. To achieve interpretable and effective robustness against TA, we propose a novel, training-free mechanistic interpretability method. Our method provides sampling-based interpretations of hidden state representations and quantitatively attributes semantic versus lexical focus to individual attention heads. Through probabilistic analysis and circuit mining, we isolate specific Vision Transformer (ViT) components that disproportionately encode lexical information, thereby identifying the mechanistic source of TA. We further show that simple interventions applied directly to the identified circuits, without any additional training, can substantially improve robustness against Typographic Attacks in object classification. These interventions, such as selective adjustment of attention weights, also outperform both supervised and training-free defense methods. Our experiments demonstrate that applying the proposed intervention to the vision encoders of several state-of-the-art LVLMs yields substantial gains in Visual Question Answering accuracy under Typographic Attack interference on RIO-Bench. These results confirm both the efficacy and the generalizability of our mechanistic approach. Code is released at https://github.com/Liu-524/SamplingTAR.
2607.02494.paper_summary_zh: 透過對比語言-圖像預訓練（CLIP）訓練的模型作為大多數現代大型視覺語言模型（LVLMs）的基礎視覺編碼器。儘管它們被廣泛採用，CLIP模型卻顯示出一種關鍵但尚未深入探討的失效模式：圖像中出現的無關文本會混淆視覺表徵，使其偏向詞彙意義而非真正的視覺語義。這一穩健性問題通常被描述為排版攻擊（TA），暴露出一種脆弱性，對於自動駕駛等安全關鍵應用構成重大風險。為了實現對TA的可解釋和有效的穩健性，我們提出了一種新穎的無需訓練的機械可解釋性方法。我們的方法提供了基於採樣的隱藏狀態表徵解釋，並定量地將語義與詞彙焦點歸因於個別注意力頭。通過概率分析和電路挖掘，我們隔離了特定的視覺Transformer（ViT）組件，這些組件不成比例地編碼詞彙信息，從而識別出TA的機械來源。我們進一步表明，對識別出的電路直接應用簡單的干預，而無需任何額外訓練，可以顯著提高對物體分類中排版攻擊的穩健性。這些干預，例如選擇性調整注意力權重，還超越了監督和無需訓練的防禦方法。我們的實驗表明，將所提出的干預應用於幾個最先進的LVLM的視覺編碼器，在排版攻擊干擾下，顯著提高了視覺問題回答的準確性，根據RIO-Bench的結果。這些結果確認了我們機械方法的有效性和普遍性。代碼已在 https://github.com/Liu-524/SamplingTAR 上發布。
